Brown Butter Banana Bread Overnight Oats Makes 4 jars ✨ 2 cups @Quaker Oats Quick 1-Minute Oats ✨ 2 cups milk ✨ 1 cup Greek yogurt ✨ 1 banana, mashed ✨ 1 tbsp + 1 tsp vanilla bean paste ✨ 1 tbsp + 1 tsp brown sugar Brown Butter Bananas: ✨ 2 tbsp butter ✨ 4 extra-ripe bananas, sliced ✨ Cinnamon, to taste ✨ 1/4 cup chopped pistachios Mix the oats, milk, yogurt, mashed banana, vanilla and brown sugar. Brown the butter in a skillet over medium heat, then lower the heat and add the sliced bananas and cinnamon. Cook for 2–3 minutes until caramelized. Divide the oats between 4 jars, layering in the bananas and pistachios as you go. Top with more bananas and pistachios, then refrigerate overnight.

For years we’ve said we’re “meal prepping for our high school athletes,” but because our boys loved popping in and out of our videos, everyone assumed we meant boys. Now both boys are in college and we’re officially cooking for the girls!

One is a rower, one is a swimmer, and they’re having a lot of fun steering the meal-prep ship. The boys were VERY steak-and-potatoes heavy 😂 The girls love that too, but they’re bringing lots of fresh ideas to the menu.

½ cup chopped pecans

½ cup melted coconut oil
½ cup dried cranberries

½ cup chia seeds

Broccoli

Maple syrup
Tomato + cucumber + red onion

VIETNAMESE LEMONGRASS CHICKEN BOWLS

6 boneless chicken thighs

MARINADE:

6 garlic cloves
1½ tsp grated ginger
3 Tbsp oyster sauce
1½ Tbsp soy sauce

1½ Tbsp honey

1½ Tbsp neutral oil

Marinate chicken at least 1 hour. Grill or sear 5–6 min/side until caramelized + cooked through.

2 Tbsp fish sauce
2 Tbsp lime juice
3 garlic cloves & bird’s eye chilies, minced

ROSEMARY CHICKEN, PARMESAN POTATOES + BROCCOLI

Chicken: Toss 3 lb chicken breasts with 3 Tbsp olive oil, 2 tsp salt, 1 tsp each pepper, garlic + onion powder, ½ tsp paprika + 2 Tbsp chopped rosemary. Seal in individual parchment packets. Bake at 375°F, 20–25 min, to 165°F.

Potatoes: Halve + score 1½ lb baby potatoes. Spread 3 Tbsp melted butter + 1 cup grated Parmesan on a sheet pan. Place potatoes cut side down; roast at 400°F, 25–30 min.

Broccoli for BOTH chicken meals: Toss florets from 2 heads with olive oil, salt, pepper + garlic powder. Roast at 400°F, 20–25 min.

TERIYAKI CHICKEN UDON + BROCCOLI

Marinate 1½ lb chicken thighs in ¾ cup soy sauce, ¼ cup each brown sugar + Shaoxing wine, 5 minced garlic cloves + 2 Tbsp minced ginger for 30 min. Remove; cook in oil, ~4 min/side, to 165°F. Chop.

In same pan, sauté ½ sliced onion, 3 cups sliced cabbage + 2 Tbsp minced garlic. Add 5 packs frozen udon, 1 cup chicken stock, 1 Tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 2 tsp sugar + a little oyster sauce + mirin. Toss to loosen noodles. Add chicken, 1 cup roasted broccoli + ½ cup shredded carrots. Top with scallions + sesame seeds.

DIN TAI FUNG-STYLE RIBS + SIDES

Mix ½ cup soy sauce, ¼ cup brown sugar, 2 Tbsp rice wine, 4 minced garlic cloves, 1 Tbsp minced ginger + 1 Tbsp sesame oil. Reserve a little; marinate 2 racks spare ribs, cut individually, in remainder for 30+ min. Roast at 350°F until tender. Boil reserved sauce + pan juices; thicken with cornstarch mixed with cold water. Brush ribs; broil ~2 min.

Toss 2 sliced English cucumbers with 3 Tbsp rice vinegar, 1 Tbsp sugar + 1 tsp each chili crisp, sesame oil + sesame seeds. Chill.

Cube 2 large sweet potatoes; toss with oil + salt. Roast at 400°F, 25–35 min.

Soy Chunk & Veggie Curry

Ingredients

* 1 cup mini soy chunks
* 1 cup curd
* ½ tsp turmeric powder
* 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
* 1 tsp garam masala
* ½ tsp coriander powder
* ½ tsp cumin powder
* 2 onions, sliced
* 6–7 garlic cloves
* 2 tsp oil
* 1 tsp cumin seeds
* 1 cup chopped vegetables
* 1 cup water
* Salt, to taste
* ½ tsp kasuri methi
* A little garam masala
* Fresh coriander, for garnish

Method

1. Add the mini soy chunks in boiling water for 5–6 minutes. Let them cool completely, then drain and squeeze out the excess water well.
2. In a bowl, add curd, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli powder, garam masala, coriander powder and cumin powder. Mix well and keep aside.
3. Heat 1 tsp oil in a pan. Add the sliced onions and garlic and sauté until golden brown. Transfer to a blender and blend into a smooth paste.
4. Heat the remaining 1 tsp oil in the same pan. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
5. Add the onion-garlic paste and the prepared curd mixture. Cook well, stirring continuously.
6. Add 1 cup water and cook until the masala comes together.
7. Add the chopped vegetables and squeezed soy chunks. Season with salt and mix well.
8. Cook for a few minutes until the curry thickens slightly and the soy chunks and vegetables absorb the masala.
9. Add kasuri methi and a little garam masala. Cook for another 1–2 minutes.
10. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with iD Malabar Parota.

On a rimmed sheet pan, toss tomatoes (cut side up), onion, and the whole garlic head with olive oil, ½ tsp salt, and pepper. Roast 40–50 minutes until edges are browned and juices run. 2. Squeeze the roasted garlic cloves out of the head. Scrape everything—including pan juices—into a pot. Stir in tomato paste and cook 1–2 minutes so it darkens slightly. 3. Calories — 500

Ingredients 🥣
2 lb or 32oz chicken breast, Raw
4 medium bell peppers (color doesn’t matter)
2 packets of  Fajita seasoning
5-second spray or ~5g avocado oil spray
2 1/2 cups or 600g cooked jasmine rice

High Protein Sauce 💪
1/2 cup or 100g nonfat plain Greek yogurt
2 tbsp or 25g sriracha
1/2 lime, juiced
Garlic powder

1️⃣ Start by getting your rice cooking in a rice cooker or pot.
2️⃣ Dice your chicken and bell peppers, then add everything to a bowl with your fajita seasoning and mix until evenly coated.

4️⃣ While that cooks, make your high-protein sauce by mixing together the Greek yogurt, sriracha, lime juice and garlic powder.
5️⃣ Once everything is cooked, evenly divide your rice, chicken and peppers between 4 meal prep containers and finish each one with your high-protein sauce.

Homemade Korean kimchi 🌶️🥬 #kimchi #koreanfood #homemadefood #foodtok #fyp 
Step-by-step guide to make traditional homemade Korean kimchi with simple ingredients and tips for fermentation. #kimchi #koreanfood #homemadefood #foodtok #fyp
Learn how to make authentic homemade Korean kimchi at home. This guide covers the key ingredients, basic preparation steps, and simple fermentation tips so you can enjoy spicy, tangy kimchi made from fresh napa cabbage.

Lead
Homemade kimchi is a staple of Korean cuisine — a fermented side dish made from napa cabbage, Korean red pepper (gochugaru), garlic, ginger, salt, and a savory seasoning paste. The process is straightforward and rewarding: salt the cabbage to draw out moisture, rinse, coat with a flavorful paste, then let it ferment until it reaches your preferred tang.

Ingredients (core items)
- Napa cabbage (large head)
- Coarse salt for brining
- Korean red pepper flakes (gochugaru)
- Garlic and fresh ginger
- Fish sauce or salted shrimp (optional for traditional flavor)
- Scallions or green onions
- Korean radish (mu) or carrot (optional)
- Sugar or fruit (small amount, optional to feed fermentation)

Basic steps
1. Prepare cabbage: Quarter the napa cabbage and salt between the leaves to start the brining process. Let sit until the leaves soften and release liquid.
2. Rinse and drain: Rinse excess salt from the cabbage and drain well so the paste will adhere.
3. Make seasoning paste: Blend gochugaru with minced garlic, grated ginger, fish sauce (or alternative), and a touch of sugar or fruit if desired. Add thinly sliced radish and scallions to the mixture.
4. Coat cabbage: Thoroughly coat each cabbage leaf with the seasoning paste by hand (use gloves if avoiding red pepper stains or irritation).
5. Pack and ferment: Pack the coated cabbage tightly into a clean jar or container, pressing down to remove air pockets. Leave some headspace, seal loosely, and let ferment at room temperature for 1–3 days depending on temperature and taste preference. Then refrigerate to slow fermentation.

Tips for success
- Use gochugaru for authentic color and flavor; adjust amount for heat level.
- Salt concentration and fermentation time control texture and sourness — shorter fermentation gives a crisper, milder kimchi; longer yields tangier results.
- Keep utensils and jars clean to avoid unwanted microbes.
- Store kimchi refrigerated after initial fermentation; flavor continues to develop slowly.

Serving suggestions
Serve kimchi as a side dish with rice, in stews and soups (kimchi jjigae), or use in fried rice, pancakes, and noodle dishes for bold flavor.

Closing
Making kimchi at home is a simple way to add a probiotic-rich, flavorful staple to your meals. Start with a small batch to dial in salt and spice levels, then experiment with fermentation time and additional ingredients to match your taste. Enjoy your homemade Korean kimchi! #kimchi #koreanfood #homemadefood #foodtok #fyp
